findings.title: Title UI fights the key art
findings.where: Title screen, center stack over the tanks and sunset background
findings.problem: The main title, subtitle, and menu box all sit on a very dark translucent panel, but the title text is oversized and the menu box is visually heavy compared with the actual action buttons. The composition feels like three separate layers competing for attention instead of one clear focal hierarchy.
findings.why: A player should instantly read the game name and the first action. Here the eye is pulled between the glowing logo, the subtitle, and the menu panel, which makes the screen feel less polished and slows first-click understanding.
findings.fix: Reduce the title block height and give the menu a lighter, thinner frame. Keep the logo as the only bright focal point, move the subtitle directly under it with smaller type, and increase the spacing between title and menu so the first selectable item is the visual secondary.

findings.title: City map has weak player/object contrast
findings.where: Open-world city screen, center play area and the ring boundary
findings.problem: The player car and many buildings are very small against a flat, cracked gray ground. The boundary circle is prominent, but the important interactable objects inside it do not separate strongly from the terrain, so the city reads more like a texture map than a navigable space.
findings.why: In a top-down game, the player needs to instantly distinguish self, destinations, and usable points of interest. If everything is similar in tone and scale, navigation feels muddy and the screen looks unfinished at a glance.
findings.fix: Increase value/color separation between the car, buildings, and ground: brighten the player vehicle outline, give each building a stronger roof silhouette, and use a more clearly tinted ground under the active city area. Add a subtle hover or marker ring to valid points of interest to make interactables read before the player moves.

findings.title: Radar reads as an empty black disc
findings.where: Arena and road screens, bottom-left HUD
findings.problem: The radar is almost entirely a dark circular void with a few tiny dots. It lacks a visible sweep, cardinal orientation cue, or stronger contact shapes, so it does not clearly communicate as a functioning sensor.
findings.why: Because it sits in a critical HUD position, players will glance here for situational awareness. If it looks inert, it weakens trust in the UI and wastes one of the most valuable at-speed information channels.
findings.fix: Add a visible rotating sweep line or pulse, enlarge enemy/POI contacts, and differentiate the player arrow from other blips with size or color. Give the disc a slightly lighter edge and a faint grid so the instrument has readable structure even when no contacts are present.

findings.title: Condition panel is too dense to parse quickly
findings.where: Arena and road screens, upper-right vertical status panel
findings.problem: The right-side condition list is a long stack of tiny green text lines with minimal grouping. Because the panel is narrow and the labels are text-heavy, the player has to read line by line to understand damage state.
findings.why: During combat or highway driving, the player needs a fast health read, not a spreadsheet. This layout makes the most important survivability information slow to scan and visually noisy.
findings.fix: Group the condition into sections with larger bars or icon rows for front/rear/left/right/underbody, and separate vital systems from detailed subsystems. Keep the numeric detail but move it to a secondary line or tooltip so the default state reads as a compact health dashboard.

findings.title: Constructor has poor hierarchy and dead space
findings.where: Vehicle constructor, especially the left list and right preview panel
findings.problem: The left side is a long text table with many values aligned in a flat column, while the right side preview occupies a large amount of unused space with a tiny car outline. The screen feels utilitarian but not well structured: the active vehicle shape is too small relative to the empty panel around it.
findings.why: This is the screen where players make consequential build decisions, so the car shape, stats, and legality feedback need a stronger visual order. Right now the layout makes it harder to connect numbers to the vehicle and feels like a prototype admin panel.
findings.fix: Increase the vehicle preview size substantially and place the key stats directly around it, not as a distant text block. Reduce the number of visible rows by grouping related parts, highlight the currently selected row with a stronger background, and use a clearer split between editable parts on the left and outcome/constraints on the right.
